title: Shot 06-packets-flowing.png is captured with the QoS panel open
evidence:
+func _on_qos_apply(pipe_id: int, alloc: Array, cls_lane: Dictionary) -> void:
+	sim.apply_command({"cmd": "set_lanes", "pipe": pipe_id, "alloc": alloc, "cls_lane": cls_lane})
+	qos_panel.open(pipe_id, sim) # re-read the applied state
---
+	main._on_qos_apply(int(spine_bundle.id), [50, 30, 20], {"email": 2, "streaming": 0})
+	# Let the sim run (main steps it per physics frame) until arcs carry traffic.
+	for i in 540:
+		await get_tree().process_frame
+	# 5 — packets streaming along the spine at class-dependent speeds.
+	_rig.frame_point(_arc_mid(spine[0], spine[1]), 1)
+	_rig.snap()
+	await _settle()
+	await _shot("06-packets-flowing.png")
detail: _on_qos_apply unconditionally re-opens the panel; _e2_shots applies lanes before the 540-frame wait and never closes the panel, so the 'packets flowing' shot includes the overlay that shot 07 exists to show.
recommended_fix: Call close_panel() (or apply the command without the panel) before the 540-frame wait; open the panel only for the 07 shot.

title: Layout computed twice despite the 'computed ONCE and threaded through' contract
evidence:
+## The ONE seeded generation body — the runtime boot AND the editor's
+## "Regenerate Preview" both run exactly this. The layout is computed ONCE
+## by the caller and threaded through, so staged nodes and sim placements
+## can never drift onto different layouts.
---
+	_generate_world(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED))
+	sim = SimCore.new()
+	sim.setup(SEED, WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED)))
detail: _ready calls wedge_layout (and node_placements) separately for staging and for sim.setup, contradicting the stated single-computation threading; node/sim alignment now rests solely on function purity, not the documented mechanism.
recommended_fix: Compute layout and placements once in _ready and pass the same instances into both _generate_world and sim.setup.

title: QoS panel fabricates node names instead of using real seeded names
evidence:
+func _node_name(idx: int) -> String:
+	return "n%02d" % (idx + 1)
---
+## `placements` = WorldSeed.node_placements() output ({name, pos, kind}).
detail: The panel invents 'n01'-style labels while placements carry a real name field and NodeSite holds site_name; SimCore.setup discards name, severing the panel from the actual node names.
recommended_fix: Pass a node-index-to-name lookup (NodeSite list or SimCore parallel array) into qos_panel.open and delete _node_name.

title: TIERS 'drawable' flag is defined but never read
detail: No line in the diff reads .drawable; _cmd_add_pipe hardcodes SimBalance.DRAW_TIER. Dead balance data implies an enforcement that does not exist.
recommended_fix: Either validate the flag where tiers become a command parameter, or remove 'drawable' from TIERS.

title: _e2_shots fetches the same sim and bundle twice under two names
evidence:

---
+	var spine_sim = main.get("sim")
+	var spine_bundle = spine_sim.bundle_for_pair(spine[0].node_index, spine[1].node_index)

title: @tool applied to planet.gd/main.gd but not node_site.gd on the same editor-preview path
evidence:
+@tool
 class_name Planet
---
@@ -8,10 +8,35 @@ extends Area3D
---
+func _regenerate_preview() -> void:
+	if not Engine.is_editor_hint():
+		return
+	_clear_generated()
+	_generate_world(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED))
---
+		var site := NodeSite.new()
+		nodes_container.add_child(site)
detail: The editor 'Regenerate Preview' path stages NodeSite instances, but node_site.gd lacks @tool, so its engine callbacks (e.g. _process pulse cooldown) never run in the editor preview — inconsistent tool coverage.
recommended_fix: Add @tool to node_site.gd with editor guards, or document why NodeSite deliberately stays non-tool on the preview path.

title: _on_rung lane fallback hardcodes lane 0 without checking it is active
evidence:
+	for cls in _cls_lane:
+		if _alloc[int(_cls_lane[cls])] <= 0:
+			var lane := SimBalance.LANE_STANDARD
+			if _alloc[lane] <= 0:
+				lane = 0
+			_cls_lane[cls] = lane
detail: The fallback assumes lane 0 is allocated; only current LADDER data guarantees it. A rung without lane 0 would pin classes to inactive lanes, producing set_lanes commands the sim silently ignores.
recommended_fix: Select the first lane with _alloc[lane] > 0 (scanning all three) instead of hardcoding LANE_STANDARD then 0.

title: Capture hardcodes site indices up to 27 with no bounds guard
detail: _e2_shots assumes at least 28 staged sites; nothing checks sites.size(). A seed or layout change with fewer placements indexes out of bounds and aborts the capture.
recommended_fix: Assert sites.size() > 27 at the top of _e2_shots, or derive the pair indices from the wedge layout.

title: Panel default _alloc/_cls_lane literals duplicate SimBalance constants and are unreachable
detail: The initial literals copy SimBalance.DEFAULT_ALLOC/DEFAULT_CLASS_LANE by hand and can never be observed — open() overwrites both before any read; silent drift if the balance table changes.
recommended_fix: Initialize from SimBalance.DEFAULT_ALLOC.duplicate() and SimBalance.DEFAULT_CLASS_LANE.duplicate(), or drop the initializers.

title: Slop-crossing motion event demotes SELECT to ORBIT without emitting its delta
evidence:
+		elif _mode == Mode.SELECT:
+			if event.position.distance_to(_press_pos) > CLICK_SLOP_PX:
+				_mode = Mode.ORBIT # a dragged select becomes an orbit
+			else:
+				return # still within click slop — no motion yet
detail: On the exact event that crosses the slop threshold the handler flips the mode but emits no orbit_moved; that motion increment is silently discarded before orbiting begins.
recommended_fix: After demoting to Mode.ORBIT, fall through to orbit_moved.emit(event.relative) for the same event.
